The double login occurs because this checkout has no reverse proxy authentication path. [Configuration](/app/conf/configuration.go) has neither proxy setting; [serveIndex](/app/server/app/serve_index.go:20) sends no authentication payload; and [authProvider](/app/ui/src/authProvider.js:7) initializes a session only after password login.

The fix belongs in those files and [auth.go](/app/server/app/auth.go:28): validate the configured header against the *actual peer address*, create a missing user on first trusted login, update `LastLoginAt`, issue a token, and send the complete auth payload only after successful authentication. [server.go](/app/server/server.go:57) applies `RealIP` before app routing, so forwarded headers need particular care at the whitelist boundary. [redactrus.go](/app/log/redactrus.go:33) also needs map and nested value redaction before the config payload can safely be logged.

There is one requirement ambiguity: it says the header user must already exist, then says to create that user on first login. I read the latter as the intended trusted first login behavior. Existing tests do not cover this feature. **No project source or tests were changed** under this diagnostic task’s scope; findings are recorded in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md).

Implemented reverse proxy login in `/app`. A configured CIDR whitelist now gates authentication using the connection’s original peer address, including IPv6 and the `@` Unix socket value. Trusted requests can use `ReverseProxyUserHeader` (default `Remote-User`) or an optional `ReverseProxyDefaultUser`. The first proxy user becomes admin; successful logins update `LastLoginAt` and send a token and Subsonic credentials for the UI to store. Untrusted requests receive no `auth` payload. Log redaction now covers nested map values and serialized auth fields.

Verification passed: focused Go tests, UI formatting check, and `git diff --check`.

VERDICT: FIX

The applied patch has two code defects:

- [Proxy login](/app/server/app/auth.go:133) accepts the result of `FindByUsername`, but [that lookup](/app/persistence/user_repository.go:75) uses SQL `LIKE`. A header username containing `%` or `_` can select a different existing user and receive that user’s token. Require an exact, case insensitive username match before issuing the token, and treat wildcard characters literally in the lookup.
- [Map redaction](/app/log/redactrus.go:63) converts every map key to a string. This changes nonstring keys and can collapse distinct keys with the same string form. Preserve the original keys while redacting values.

Relevant existing tests **passed**:

- `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./server/app ./log ./conf ./server` (`conf` has no test files)
- `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./persistence ./server/subsonic`
- `CI=true npm test -- --watch=false --runInBand` in `/app/ui` — 10 suites, 34 tests

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** none. This was an independent review; no project code was changed.

Fixed both review findings. Username lookup now treats `%` and `_` literally while remaining case insensitive, and proxy login checks the returned username before issuing a token. Map redaction now preserves original key types and redacts nested values. Added regression tests for both.

All three reviewer-listed test commands passed: the Go package groups and the UI suite (10 suites, 34 tests). No test environment problems remain.
